newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market slow, rate rise on cards.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market slow, rate rise on cards.

text.p: Croatian money market trade was slow on Monday on poor kuna supply as banks' accounts sank to the lowest level since before last summer, dealers said.
"The banks' accounts are practically drained," one dealer told Reuters, indicating that a rate rise may be on the cards.
Fresh trade totalled only 12 million kuna, with a surplus five million left in supply as creditors and borrowers could not agree on terms.
Creditors were also said to have been draining funds for the earlier granted loans and the central bank drained back 32.8 million kuna granted to the banking sector on Feb 7.
Roughly one half of new borrowings were interbank call money loans at 10.5 and 12 percent, the latter price being readily paid by a bank with tight kuna liquidity.
"This move might also point to a pending rise in (money market) rates," the dealer said.
One three-week six million kuna loan was granted by the Croatian Bank for Reconstruction and Development (HBOR) at an 11-percent rate.
The weekend overnight borrowings by six banks seeking to maintain their mandatory reserves totalled 30.7 million kuna. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
